Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 26735dfdd8930d9ef1fa92e590a9bf77726efdf6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 13:13:31 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] pmdomain: core: Fix detach procedure for virtual devices in
 genpd

If a device is attached to a PM domain through genpd_dev_pm_attach_by_id(),
genpd calls pm_runtime_enable() for the corresponding virtual device that
it registers. While this avoids boilerplate code in drivers, there is no
corresponding call to pm_runtime_disable() in genpd_dev_pm_detach().

This means these virtual devices are typically detached from its genpd,
while runtime PM remains enabled for them, which is not how things are
designed to work. In worst cases it may lead to critical errors, like a
NULL pointer dereference bug in genpd_runtime_suspend(), which was recently
reported. For another case, we may end up keeping an unnecessary vote for a
performance state for the device.

To fix these problems, let's add this missing call to pm_runtime_disable()
in genpd_dev_pm_detach().

Reported-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert@linux-m68k.org>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/CAMuHMdWapT40hV3c+CSBqFOW05aWcV1a6v_NiJYgoYi0i9_PDQ@mail.gmail.com/
Fixes: 3c095f32a92b ("PM / Domains: Add support for multi PM domains per device to genpd")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Tested-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/pmdomain/core.c b/drivers/pmdomain/core.c
index 4d32fc676aaf..71e930e80178 100644
--- a/drivers/pmdomain/core.c
+++ b/drivers/pmdomain/core.c
@@ -3089,6 +3089,7 @@ static const struct bus_type genpd_bus_type = {
 static void genpd_dev_pm_detach(struct device *dev, bool power_off)
 {
 	struct generic_pm_domain *pd;
+	bool is_virt_dev;
 	unsigned int i;
 	int ret = 0;
 
@@ -3098,6 +3099,13 @@ static void genpd_dev_pm_detach(struct device *dev, bool power_off)
 
 	dev_dbg(dev, "removing from PM domain %s\n", pd->name);
 
+	/* Check if the device was created by genpd at attach. */
+	is_virt_dev = dev->bus == &genpd_bus_type;
+
+	/* Disable runtime PM if we enabled it at attach. */
+	if (is_virt_dev)
+		pm_runtime_disable(dev);
+
 	/* Drop the default performance state */
 	if (dev_gpd_data(dev)->default_pstate) {
 		dev_pm_genpd_set_performance_state(dev, 0);
@@ -3123,7 +3131,7 @@ static void genpd_dev_pm_detach(struct device *dev, bool power_off)
 	genpd_queue_power_off_work(pd);
 
 	/* Unregister the device if it was created by genpd. */
-	if (dev->bus == &genpd_bus_type)
+	if (is_virt_dev)
 		device_unregister(dev);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies `drivers/pmdomain/core.c` to fix a missing `pm_runtime_disable()` call during detach of virtual devices (those created by `genpd_dev_pm_attach_by_id()`). The changes are:

1. Introduces a local boolean variable `is_virt_dev` to identify virtual devices by checking if their bus type is `genpd_bus_type`.
2. Adds a call to `pm_runtime_disable(dev)` for virtual devices at the start of the detach procedure, since runtime PM was enabled during attach.
3. Replaces the subsequent inline bus check with the already-computed `is_virt_dev` for consistency when deciding to call `device_unregister()`.

These modifications ensure that runtime PM is properly disabled for virtual devices when they are detached from a PM domain, preventing issues such as NULL pointer dereferences or stale performance state votes. The boolean variable also makes the code cleaner by avoiding redundant checks.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
static void genpd_dev_pm_detach(struct device *dev, bool power_off)
{
    // ... (no pm_runtime_disable call before the fix)
}
```
Reason:
The `genpd_dev_pm_detach()` function lacks a corresponding `pm_runtime_disable()` to balance the `pm_runtime_enable()` that was performed earlier in `genpd_dev_pm_attach_by_id()` for virtual devices. This imbalance leaves runtime PM enabled on virtual devices after detachment, causing issues such as NULL pointer dereference in `genpd_runtime_suspend()` and unnecessary performance state votes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
+	bool is_virt_dev;
...
+	/* Check if the device was created by genpd at attach. */
+	is_virt_dev = dev->bus == &genpd_bus_type;
+
+	/* Disable runtime PM if we enabled it at attach. */
+	if (is_virt_dev)
+		pm_runtime_disable(dev);
```
Reason:
The fix identifies virtual devices by checking if their bus type is `genpd_bus_type`, then calls `pm_runtime_disable()` to properly balance the earlier `pm_runtime_enable()`. This prevents the runtime PM state from remaining enabled on detached virtual devices, avoiding the reported NULL pointer dereference and other side effects.
